variables.name: BOXER_ADHOC_DIR
variables.description: directory whose filesystem holds the unnamed sealed files of ad-hoc datasets, staged recordings and window captures (ADR-0240 §SD1, ADR-0281); empty resolves to <user cache dir>/boxer/adhoc; must support O_TMPFILE (ext4, tmpfs)

variables.name: BOXER_ADR_DIR
variables.description: ADR markdown directory to read as the corpus; empty finds the nearest doc/adr at or above the working directory

variables.name: BOXER_ADR_ROOT
variables.description: source tree to scan for ADR code citations; empty derives the checkout containing the ADR directory, and an unresolvable root just omits the code evidence

variables.name: BOXER_AGENTCONSOLE_DESTINATIONS
variables.description: comma-separated grant destinations in the agent console's field when a window opens; for scenes and demos

variables.name: BOXER_AGENT_ACTIONS_FILE
variables.description: file the headless host appends every runtime.agent action record to, as JSON lines, for trials (ADR-0269); honoured only on the headless host

variables.name: BOXER_AGENT_CALLS_MAX
variables.description: the largest call budget the person can give a new runtime.agent task in the host's approval dialog; a budget a coordinator asks for above it is lowered to it

variables.name: BOXER_AGENT_CALLS_MIN
variables.description: the least call budget the person can give a new runtime.agent task in the host's approval dialog; a budget a coordinator asks for below it is raised to it

variables.name: BOXER_AGENT_COORDINATORS
variables.description: comma-separated app ids or subject aliases allowed to ask the person for an agent task grant (ADR-0269), e.g. chat,agentconsole; empty allows none

variables.name: BOXER_AGENT_COORDINATORS_WHERE
variables.description: ClickHouse boolean expression over keelson.apps columns; the launchable apps it selects at boot may ask the person for an agent task grant, beside those BOXER_AGENT_COORDINATORS names (ADR-0364, proposed), e.g. kind = 'chatlet'. Unset selects none; set and not evaluable, the host does not boot

variables.name: BOXER_AGENT_DEADLINE
variables.description: how long a runtime.agent task runs before its calls wait for the person to give it more time, and how much more an approval gives

variables.name: BOXER_AGENT_PACE
variables.description: the least time between two visible changes — a change to a window, a window opened, an arrangement — of a runtime.agent task whose coordinator's ceiling does not let the model work unpaced

variables.name: BOXER_AGENT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT
variables.description: how long a runtime.agent grant request or widening waits in the person's dialog before it expires; the coordinator's call waits as long

variables.name: BOXER_AGENT_TEST_GRANTS
variables.description: issue runtime.agent task grants without the person's approval, for scenes and tests (ADR-0269); honoured only on the headless host

variables.name: BOXER_AGENT_UNATTENDED
variables.description: turn on the unattended mode (ADR-0298): the host approves runtime.agent grant requests and widenings and accepts suggest-mode proposals in the person's place, within the coordinator's ceiling, BOXER_AGENT_CALLS_MAX and BOXER_AGENT_DEADLINE; a spent budget, a passed deadline and a consequential command still wait for the person; honoured only by a binary built with the boxer_unattended tag

variables.name: BOXER_ANCHOR_STORE_PASSWORD
variables.description: password for BOXER_ANCHOR_STORE_URL

variables.name: BOXER_ANCHOR_STORE_TABLE
variables.description: database-qualified table the anchor store holds the heads in; created where absent

variables.name: BOXER_ANCHOR_STORE_URL
variables.description: HTTP endpoint of the organisation's ClickHouse anchor store (ADR-0314 §SD2); unset anchors heads in memory, not durably

variables.name: BOXER_ANCHOR_STORE_USER
variables.description: user for BOXER_ANCHOR_STORE_URL

variables.name: BOXER_ATTENTION_AWAY_IDLE
variables.description: how long the host waits without the person's input before it sets them Away: cards stop opening on their own and an away log is kept, shown when Away ends — at the next input; 0 never

variables.name: BOXER_ATTENTION_ESCALATE
variables.description: how long a decision waits in the person's queue unacknowledged before its card opens on its own; an item this close to its expiry is marked; 0 never escalates

variables.name: BOXER_ATTENTION_FLOOD_PERSON
variables.description: how many decisions all conversations together may ask of the person in ten minutes; the next is refused with a reason the model can act on; 0 does not bound

variables.name: BOXER_ATTENTION_FLOOD_STREAM
variables.description: how many decisions one conversation may ask of the person in ten minutes; the next is refused with a reason the model can act on; 0 does not bound

variables.name: BOXER_ATTENTION_OPEN_OWN
variables.description: open the card of a grant request, widening or confirmation at once when the window asking is the active one or the one the person last gave input to; off, it waits in the queue like any item until BOXER_ATTENTION_ESCALATE

variables.name: BOXER_AUDIO_PEAKS_CACHE_DIR
variables.description: directory holding cached audio peaks pyramids (ADR-0208 §SD4); empty uses <user cache dir>/boxer/audio-peaks

variables.name: BOXER_CAPMAP_VAULT
variables.description: business-capability vault directory to read as the corpus; empty finds the nearest doc/competences at or above the working directory

variables.name: BOXER_CELL_APPROVALS
variables.description: the approval path for an exit above a sink's clearance, per TLP tier, as TIER=path pairs separated by commas; a path is free, person (a recorded justification), organisation (an approver) or never (ADR-0312 §SD3)

variables.name: BOXER_CELL_CANARIES
variables.description: planted canary tokens (ADR-0312 §SD6) as scope=token@TIER triples separated by commas: an outbound payload that contains a token of a tier above the sink's clearance is refused; a triple without a tier is RED

variables.name: BOXER_CELL_CLIPBOARD_CLEARANCE
variables.description: the TLP clearance of the clipboard out of boxer (ADR-0312 §SD1, ADR-0317): the highest tier that copies as plaintext without an approval

variables.name: BOXER_CELL_CONFINED_TIER
variables.description: the TLP tier content labelled confined (derived from sealed data) carries at the sinks (ADR-0311 §SD1): a deployment default, not fixed by boxer; a value that names no tier fails closed to RED, where a clearance that names none fails to CLEAR

variables.name: BOXER_CELL_EGRESS_CLEARANCE
variables.description: the TLP clearance of an HTTP egress destination outside the cell (ADR-0312 §SD1): the highest tier the outbound half of a fetch may carry

variables.name: BOXER_CELL_EXPORT_CLEARANCE
variables.description: the TLP clearance of file export and printing (ADR-0312 §SD1): the highest tier that leaves as a file without an approval

variables.name: BOXER_CELL_MANAGED
variables.description: the host is managed by the organisation (ADR-0307 §SD6): exits above the policy on relay channels are prevented, where on a host the person administers they are recorded and not prevented

variables.name: BOXER_CELL_PEERS
variables.description: peer cells of the same organisation and the TLP clearance of what is sent to each, as name=TIER pairs separated by commas (ADR-0307 §SD2, ADR-0312 §SD1)

variables.name: BOXER_CELL_ROUTE_CLEARANCE
variables.description: the TLP clearance of a remote model route (ADR-0312 §SD1): the highest tier a request may carry to a model host outside the cell; a loopback or trusted host is inside the cell and has none

variables.name: BOXER_CHAT_ADVANCED
variables.description: fill the chat app's Analytics tab — token and answer statistics of the window's conversations, the conversation's agent surface, and Open in play on them as ad-hoc datasets; false leaves the tab saying how to turn it on

variables.name: BOXER_CHAT_ALLOW
variables.description: the highest action a new chat window's settings start at: read, view, edit, run or outside (publishes and exports, each still confirmed unless the grant lists its destination); the person can move it in the chat's Settings

variables.name: BOXER_CHAT_APPS
variables.description: turn on Apps in a new chat window: the model may ask the person for windows to work in (ADR-0269); a chat listed in BOXER_AGENT_COORDINATORS starts with Apps on anyway

variables.name: BOXER_CHAT_ARTEFACT
variables.description: turn on the Artefact in a new chat window: one markdown document per conversation that the model edits through tools (ADR-0282); for scenes and demos

variables.name: BOXER_CHAT_CALL_WAIT
variables.description: how long a chat's tool call waits for its operation to settle, when it does not wait on the person; after that an asynchronous operation is followed in the background and any other reports the phase it reached (ADR-0358)

variables.name: BOXER_CHAT_DRAFT
variables.description: text in the chat app's composer when a window opens; for scenes and demos

variables.name: BOXER_CHAT_IMAGE_BYTES
variables.description: the most a chat conversation's screenshots may hold on disk, in bytes of their sealed files (ADR-0284); a capture, copy or crop past it is refused

variables.name: BOXER_CHAT_IMAGE_COUNT
variables.description: the most screenshots a chat conversation's artefact may name (ADR-0284)

variables.name: BOXER_CHAT_IMAGE_PIXELS
variables.description: the most pixels a chat screenshot may have; a PNG past it is refused from its header, before it is decoded (ADR-0284)

variables.name: BOXER_CHAT_OPERATION_TOOLS
variables.description: offer each operation of a window in the chat's task as its own typed tool, w<window>_<operation>, beside call_operation; for trials

variables.name: BOXER_CHAT_PENDING_MAX
variables.description: how long a chat follows an asynchronous operation in the background before it records that no end was seen (ADR-0358)

variables.name: BOXER_CHAT_PIXELS
variables.description: the Pixels level of a new chat window — which of the artefact's screenshots the model may see, and with whose consent (ADR-0287): none, ask, ask-once or captures; for scenes and demos

variables.name: BOXER_CHAT_PIXELS_LOCAL
variables.description: turn on Only to a local model in a new chat window: screenshots are sent only to a model on this machine or one the host trusts with sealed data (ADR-0287); for scenes and demos

variables.name: BOXER_CHAT_PIXELS_LOCAL_REQUIRED
variables.description: require Only to a local model in every chat on this host (ADR-0287): screenshots reach only a model on this machine or one the host trusts with sealed data, and the person cannot turn it off

variables.name: BOXER_CHAT_PIXELS_MAX
variables.description: the highest Pixels level a chat on this host may use (ADR-0287): none, ask, ask-once or captures; the person cannot set a chat above it

variables.name: BOXER_CHAT_PROFILE
variables.description: the harness profile a chat runs under — the tool set, prompt book, seam elements, route and constants as one named, fingerprinted value (ADR-0310); default is the only profile registered

variables.name: BOXER_CHAT_QUESTIONS
variables.description: turn on Questions in a new chat window: the model may ask the person structured questions as an inline form (ask_user); for scenes and demos

variables.name: BOXER_CHAT_ROUNDS
variables.description: the rounds of model calls a chat turn with tools starts with in a new chat window, within BOXER_CHAT_ROUNDS_MIN and BOXER_CHAT_ROUNDS_MAX; the person can move it in the chat's Settings

variables.name: BOXER_CHAT_ROUNDS_MAX
variables.description: the most rounds of model calls a chat turn with tools may be given in the chat's Settings

variables.name: BOXER_CHAT_ROUNDS_MIN
variables.description: the fewest rounds of model calls a chat turn with tools may be given in the chat's Settings; the last round of a turn offers no tools, so it ends with an answer

variables.name: BOXER_CHAT_WAKES_MAX
variables.description: how many turns finished background work may start in a chat since the person last spoke; past it, results wait for their next message, and 0 means they always do (ADR-0358)

variables.name: BOXER_CLICKHOUSE_BINARY_PATH
variables.description: path to the clickhouse binary used by leeway DDL test utilities

variables.name: BOXER_CLICKHOUSE_LOCAL
variables.description: explicit path to the clickhouse binary `clickhouse local` runs; empty uses the PATH lookup

variables.name: BOXER_COMPONENT
variables.description: component identity mark, injected by the supervisor (unit Environment= line, launcher script) and inherited by children; read by the topology layer (ADR-0126); empty = unmarked

variables.name: BOXER_FAIRLEAD_JOURNAL_DIR
variables.description: directory each process appends one JSON line per distinct SQL statement it sends to (file `<pid>-<start>.jsonl`); empty records nothing. Statement text is written as sent, bound values excluded and inlined literals included, so the directory is as sensitive as the queries

variables.name: BOXER_FFPROBE_BIN
variables.description: explicit path to the ffprobe binary the audio decoder spawns; empty uses the PATH lookup

variables.name: BOXER_FIBSCOPE_ID
variables.description: the 64-bit word a new fibscope window opens on, decimal or 0x-prefixed hexadecimal; a word that is not a tagged id is accepted; for scenes and demos

variables.name: BOXER_FLIGHT_RECORDER
variables.description: enable the Go runtime flight recorder

variables.name: BOXER_FLIGHT_RECORDER_OUTPUT_FILE
variables.description: destination path for the flight recorder trace dump

variables.name: BOXER_FS_APPDATA_DIR
variables.description: fs broker: root of the per-app data areas (fs.appdata.*); empty uses <user config dir>/boxer/appdata

variables.name: BOXER_GODEP_ROOT
variables.description: module directory the keelson go_packages/go_imports tables collect from; empty resolves the nearest go.mod above the working directory

variables.name: BOXER_GODEP_TAGS
variables.description: comma-separated build tags for the keelson go_packages/go_imports collection; empty falls back to <root>/tags then inherited GOFLAGS

variables.name: BOXER_GRIB_CORPUS
variables.description: directory of GRIB survey corpora with oracle dumps, and the WMO table checkouts, for the integration lane and the table generator

variables.name: BOXER_IMZERO_DEBUG_MODE
variables.description: imzero2 debug profile: memcheck|massif|flamegraph|heaptrack; empty uses the default launcher

variables.name: BOXER_JACKSTAY_PLAN
variables.description: jackstay window: plan, by file name in the window's data area (fs.appdata), opened at start and saved to (created on first save when missing)

variables.name: BOXER_JACKSTAY_TARGET_ENDPOINT
variables.description: jackstay target server: HTTP URL or host:port (e.g. http://replica:8123/); empty means no target

variables.name: BOXER_JACKSTAY_TARGET_PASSWORD
variables.description: jackstay target server password; read from the environment only, never stored in a plan

variables.name: BOXER_JACKSTAY_TARGET_USER
variables.description: jackstay target server user

variables.name: BOXER_KAFKA_BROKERS
variables.description: comma-separated list of broker addresses (host1:9092,host2:9092)

variables.name: BOXER_KAFKA_CLIENT_ID
variables.description: kafka client.id

variables.name: BOXER_KAFKA_SASL_MECHANISM
variables.description: SASL mechanism: none, PLAIN, SCRAM-SHA-256, SCRAM-SHA-512 or OAUTHBEARER (case-insensitive); unset means none

variables.name: BOXER_KAFKA_SASL_PASSWORD
variables.description: SASL password (PLAIN, SCRAM-SHA-256, SCRAM-SHA-512); prefer the variable to the flag, which lands in shell history

variables.name: BOXER_KAFKA_SASL_TOKEN
variables.description: static OAUTHBEARER token (only for --sasl-mechanism=OAUTHBEARER)

variables.name: BOXER_KAFKA_SASL_USERNAME
variables.description: SASL username (PLAIN, SCRAM-SHA-256, SCRAM-SHA-512)

variables.name: BOXER_KAFKA_TLS
variables.description: enable TLS (implicit if any --tls-* file flag is set)

variables.name: BOXER_KAFKA_TLS_CA_FILE
variables.description: path to a PEM-encoded CA bundle for verifying the broker certificate

variables.name: BOXER_KAFKA_TLS_CERT_FILE
variables.description: path to a PEM-encoded client certificate (for mTLS); requires --tls-key-file

variables.name: BOXER_KAFKA_TLS_KEY_FILE
variables.description: path to a PEM-encoded client key (for mTLS); requires --tls-cert-file

variables.name: BOXER_KAFKA_TLS_SKIP_VERIFY
variables.description: skip broker certificate verification (insecure; useful for self-signed dev clusters)

variables.name: BOXER_LADING_PUBLISH_BYTES
variables.description: the most bytes of files one publish into the lading store may carry (ADR-0341); a larger tree is refused, not split

variables.name: BOXER_LADING_PUBLISH_MAX_DAYS
variables.description: the longest retention class, in days, a publish into the lading store may name (ADR-0341)

variables.name: BOXER_LADING_PUBLISH_TIER
variables.description: the highest TLP tier a tree published into the lading store may carry (ADR-0341); everyone who can read the store reads what is in it, and a confined tree is refused whatever this says

variables.name: BOXER_LAUNCHER_FRECENCY_HALFLIFE
variables.description: launcher ranking decay: a launch this old counts half as much as one just now

variables.name: BOXER_LLM_APIKEY
variables.description: API key the host's llm service sends to the endpoint; empty for local endpoints that take none

variables.name: BOXER_LLM_CONTEXT_TOKENS
variables.description: the model's context size in tokens, reported by llm.describe so a chat can say how full its conversation is; 0 asks the endpoint's model list once at start (context_length, max_model_len and the like), and a server that reports none leaves it unknown

variables.name: BOXER_LLM_ENDPOINT
variables.description: OpenAI-compatible chat-completions base URL the host's llm service talks to (e.g. http://localhost:1234/v1); unset means no model is offered to apps

variables.name: BOXER_LLM_MAXTOKENS
variables.description: completion token ceiling per llm.complete when the request names none

variables.name: BOXER_LLM_MODEL
variables.description: model id the host's llm service completes with; unset means no model is offered even with the endpoint set

variables.name: BOXER_LLM_MODERATORS
variables.description: comma-separated app ids that may set, list and cancel through llm.ration.* (ADR-0300): the moderators that throttle and refuse model calls; empty means no app may

variables.name: BOXER_LLM_RATION_UNRULED
variables.description: what the llm service does when its usage ledger could not be rebuilt from boxer.facts at start: allow (serve, counting from zero) or refuse (refuse every model call until restart)

variables.name: BOXER_LLM_RETAIN
variables.description: ceiling on keeping model message text: off (sizes and counts only), ring (text on this process's keelson('llm_calls') rows), durable (ring, plus the messages of llm.retain.* requests on boxer.facts, kept until removed by hand)

variables.name: BOXER_LLM_SCRIPT
variables.description: path to a scripted model (JSON lines, one reply each; "$name" in an argument takes the last value a tool result gave name) the llm service answers from instead of an endpoint; honoured only on the headless host, for scenes

variables.name: BOXER_LLM_TIMEOUT
variables.description: wall-clock bound on one llm.complete; the service cancels the provider call at it, and app clients that name no timeout of their own wait that long plus a few seconds for the reply

variables.name: BOXER_LLM_TRUSTED_HOSTS
variables.description: comma-separated endpoint host names or IPs, without port, that the llm service treats like loopback: confined (sealed) content may be sent to them; list only machines under your own control, and prefer an https endpoint

variables.name: BOXER_LOGVIEWER_REFRESH
variables.description: how often an open log viewer window re-reads its rows from boxer.facts in the background; the Refresh button reads at once; under 1s reads every second

variables.name: BOXER_LOGVIEWER_ROWS
variables.description: how many of the newest matching log rows a log viewer window keeps in memory and shows; bounds each read from boxer.facts; clamped to 100..100000

variables.name: BOXER_LOG_CALLER
variables.description: include caller file:line in log records

variables.name: BOXER_LOG_COLOR
variables.description: colorize console log output (auto-detects TTY when unset; off for file destinations)

variables.name: BOXER_LOG_CORRELATION_ID
variables.description: correlation id for log records; empty seeds a nanoid(21)

variables.name: BOXER_LOG_FACTS
variables.description: non-empty (and not "0") persists the host's log lines to boxer.facts through the ClickHouse store, which is where the log viewer reads them; empty/0 persists none, and the log viewer says so

variables.name: BOXER_LOG_FACTS_URL
variables.description: overrides the chstore default ClickHouse URL when BOXER_LOG_FACTS is enabled

variables.name: BOXER_LOG_FILE
variables.description: path to the log file; empty or "-" routes to stderr

variables.name: BOXER_LOG_FORMAT
variables.description: log output format

variables.name: BOXER_LOG_LEVEL
variables.description: zerolog level

variables.name: BOXER_LOG_MODULE_INFO_ON_START
variables.description: log the Go module info on application startup

variables.name: BOXER_LOG_OS_ARGS_ON_START
variables.description: log os.Args on application startup

variables.name: BOXER_LOG_OS_HOST_ON_START
variables.description: log the host name on application startup

variables.name: BOXER_LOG_OS_PID_ON_START
variables.description: log the OS process id on application startup

variables.name: BOXER_LOG_VCS_REVISION_ON_START
variables.description: log the VCS revision on application startup

variables.name: BOXER_MAP_TILE_ATTRIBUTION
variables.description: attribution/credit line rendered over the basemap; empty shows none. Defaults to OpenStreetMap's required credit, which stays correct for a mirror of OSM tiles — a different tile source needs whatever credit line its terms of use require.

variables.name: BOXER_MAP_TILE_ATTRIBUTION_URL
variables.description: link target behind BOXER_MAP_TILE_ATTRIBUTION; empty renders the credit as plain text. Defaults to the OpenStreetMap copyright page.

variables.name: BOXER_MAP_TILE_CA_FILE
variables.description: path to a PEM certificate bundle added to the trust roots when fetching from BOXER_MAP_TILE_URL, for a tile server behind an internal CA; certificate verification stays on. Must hold the issuing CA — a bare self-signed server certificate is not accepted as its own trust anchor, and needs BOXER_MAP_TILE_INSECURE_TLS instead. Ignored unless BOXER_MAP_TILE_URL is set explicitly, and superseded by BOXER_MAP_TILE_INSECURE_TLS.

variables.name: BOXER_MAP_TILE_INSECURE_TLS
variables.description: disable TLS certificate verification for BOXER_MAP_TILE_URL tile requests. Accepts any certificate, so it also accepts an interceptor's: use it only against a tile server you control on a trusted network, and prefer BOXER_MAP_TILE_CA_FILE. Also drops the protocol floor to TLS 1.0 and admits the legacy cipher suites (static-RSA key exchange, 3DES, RC4), so an old server is reachable rather than failing on version or cipher negotiation — once the peer is unauthenticated neither one protects anything. Ignored unless BOXER_MAP_TILE_URL is set explicitly — it never applies to the default OpenStreetMap server.

variables.name: BOXER_MAP_TILE_MAX_ZOOM
variables.description: highest zoom level served by BOXER_MAP_TILE_URL (1..255); 0 keeps the widget default. Defaults to 19, which is what OpenStreetMap serves.

variables.name: BOXER_MAP_TILE_URL
variables.description: XYZ tile-server URL template for slippy-map basemaps, e.g. "http://mygis/{z}/{x}/{y}.png"; must contain the {z}/{x}/{y} placeholders. Defaults to OpenStreetMap, which fetches tiles from tile.openstreetmap.org over the public internet — set this to a self-hosted GIS to keep basemap traffic inside the deployment. Setting it is also what enables the BOXER_MAP_TILE_*_TLS / _CA_FILE knobs.

variables.name: BOXER_MARKDOWN_ECHO
variables.description: echo os.Args as a markdown shell code block on startup (experimental)

variables.name: BOXER_MDEDIT_DOC
variables.description: markdown for a new mdedit window to open as an unsaved document of its own, neither restored nor autosaved; for scenes and demos

variables.name: BOXER_MODERATOR
variables.description: run the host's built-in moderator (ADR-0302): it watches model calls and agent actions for loops and slows, then stops, the windows that loop; true also lists it in BOXER_LLM_MODERATORS

variables.name: BOXER_PLAY_ALLOW_WRITES
variables.description: non-empty lets Run execute an INSERT … SELECT wrapper (ADR-0181 §SD8) and DDL; unset, Run refuses the write with a copy-out hint and every Arrow run is sent readonly=2. Governs every play-engined host, sqlapplet included

variables.name: BOXER_PLAY_APP_WRITES
variables.description: "off" stops play writing its own tables — the Series verdicts in boxer.tslabels; unset or anything else lets it (ADR-0270 §SD7). BOXER_PLAY_ALLOW_WRITES does not govern them

variables.name: BOXER_PLAY_AUTORUN

variables.name: BOXER_PLAY_DOCK_SPLITS
variables.description: initial dock split fractions, as comma-separated zone=fraction pairs (zones: editor, tools, side, bottom; fraction in (0,1), the share the leaf split from keeps — editor=0.3 gives the editor row 30% of the height); unnamed zones keep their default; a malformed pair fails the mount

variables.name: BOXER_PLAY_EXIT_ON_SHOT

variables.name: BOXER_PLAY_FOCUS_BOWTIE
variables.description: non-empty makes Bow-tie the default-active tab in its dock leaf (scripted screenshots)

variables.name: BOXER_PLAY_FOCUS_CARDS
variables.description: non-empty makes Cards the default-active tab in its dock leaf (scripted screenshots)

variables.name: BOXER_PLAY_FOCUS_CHART
variables.description: non-empty makes Chart the default-active tab in its dock leaf (scripted screenshots)

variables.name: BOXER_PLAY_FOCUS_CHAT
variables.description: non-empty makes Chat the default-active tab in its dock leaf (scripted screenshots)

variables.name: BOXER_PLAY_FOCUS_COMPLETION
variables.description: non-empty makes Completion the default-active tab in its dock leaf (scripted screenshots)

variables.name: BOXER_PLAY_FOCUS_DETAIL
variables.description: non-empty makes Detail the default-active tab in its dock leaf (scripted screenshots)

variables.name: BOXER_PLAY_FOCUS_DIAGNOSTICS
variables.description: non-empty makes Diagnostics the default-active tab in its dock leaf (scripted screenshots)

variables.name: BOXER_PLAY_FOCUS_DIST
variables.description: non-empty makes Distribution the default-active tab in its dock leaf (scripted screenshots)

variables.name: BOXER_PLAY_FOCUS_DOCS
variables.description: non-empty makes Docs the default-active tab in its dock leaf (scripted screenshots)

variables.name: BOXER_PLAY_FOCUS_EDITOR
variables.description: non-empty makes Editor the default-active tab in its dock leaf (scripted screenshots)

variables.name: BOXER_PLAY_FOCUS_FILES
variables.description: non-empty makes Files the default-active tab in its dock leaf (scripted screenshots)

variables.name: BOXER_PLAY_FOCUS_FLOW
variables.description: non-empty makes Flow the default-active tab in its dock leaf (scripted screenshots)

variables.name: BOXER_PLAY_FOCUS_GLOSSES
variables.description: non-empty makes Glosses the default-active tab in its dock leaf (scripted screenshots)

variables.name: BOXER_PLAY_FOCUS_GRAPH
variables.description: non-empty makes Graph the default-active tab in its dock leaf (scripted screenshots)

variables.name: BOXER_PLAY_FOCUS_GRAPHVIEW
variables.description: non-empty makes Graphview the default-active tab in its dock leaf (scripted screenshots)

variables.description: non-empty makes History the default-active tab in its dock leaf (scripted screenshots)

variables.description: non-empty makes Icicle the default-active tab in its dock leaf (scripted screenshots)

variables.name: BOXER_PLAY_MAP_CENTER
variables.description: initial Map center as "lat,lon" (WGS84); empty or unparseable keeps the default (40,0)

variables.name: BOXER_PLAY_MAP_SIZE
variables.description: pin a fixed Map widget size as "WxH" logical points (deterministic scripted screenshots); empty or unparseable keeps the default (the map fills the Map tab)

variables.name: BOXER_PLAY_MAP_TABLE
variables.description: initial table for the Map panel; empty keeps the default (planes_mercator_sample100)

variables.name: BOXER_PLAY_MAP_ZOOM
variables.description: initial Map zoom level; a positive value overrides the default (4)

variables.name: BOXER_PLAY_OBSERVE
variables.description: graph node id to observe in the result panels after a Run (scripted screenshots); silently ignored when the node is absent from the split

variables.name: BOXER_PLAY_PREVIEW_AS_SENT
variables.description: non-empty starts the Preview tab in 'as sent to server' mode (post-pass wire SQL) for scripted screenshots

variables.name: BOXER_PLAY_SCREENSHOT
variables.description: if set, the play HMI captures a screenshot to this path after the first frame

variables.name: BOXER_PLAY_SHOT_SETTLE
variables.description: settle frames before BOXER_PLAY_SCREENSHOT fires; a positive value overrides the default (5), e.g. to wait out an async panel fetch

variables.name: BOXER_PLAY_SQL
variables.description: initial SQL buffer for the play HMI; non-empty wins over the persisted-session restore

variables.name: BOXER_PLAY_TAB_ZONES
variables.description: re-zone tabs at launch, as comma-separated id=zone pairs (zones: body, editor, tools, side, bottom; id * names every tab; later pairs win), e.g. "*=body" for one full-panel leaf; a pair naming an unknown tab or zone fails the mount

variables.name: BOXER_PLAY_TIMELINE_BANDS_SQL
variables.description: panel-local bands SQL for the Timeline tab; non-empty wins over the persisted-session restore

variables.name: BOXER_PLAY_WINDOW_SIZE
variables.description: open the play window at "WxH" logical points (scripted screenshots); empty or unparseable keeps the host's archetype default

variables.name: BOXER_RCLONE
variables.description: explicit path to the rclone binary the lading store's SFTP seam spawns; empty uses the PATH lookup

variables.name: BOXER_RUN_DRIVER_ATTEMPT
variables.description: the attempt of the benchmark take BOXER_RUN_DRIVER_JOB names, a uint32, written as the run row's driver attempt

variables.name: BOXER_RUN_DRIVER_JOB
variables.description: the benchmark take a window host runs, named suite/task/take; set, the host's run row names driver bench and this job

variables.name: BOXER_RUN_DRIVER_JOB_KIND
variables.description: the suite version of the benchmark take BOXER_RUN_DRIVER_JOB names, written as the run row's driver job kind

variables.name: BOXER_RUN_ID
variables.description: per-process run id; inherited from a parent process when set, otherwise generated by Init()

variables.name: BOXER_SQLAPPLETCREATOR_DRAFT
variables.description: a draft for a new SQL applet creator window, as JSON with Sql and Endpoint (as the launch config carries them) and Slug, Title, Summary and Icon; a caller's launch config wins over it; for scenes and demos

variables.name: BOXER_SQLAPPLET_DATASET_EVENTS
variables.description: dataset binder event path (ADR-0188 §SD3): on = subscribe and act; drop = subscribe but discard, reconcile alone binds (fault injection); off = do not subscribe, poll

variables.name: BOXER_SQLAPPLET_DATASET_RECONCILE
variables.description: dataset binder reconcile interval with events subscribed (ADR-0188 §SD3); a Go duration such as 30s or 5s

variables.name: BOXER_SQLAPPLET_TAB_DOC
variables.description: a browser tab fetches this applet document from its page's origin and mounts it (ADR-0299): a path relative to the page, such as applets/x.md, or absolute on its origin, such as /applets/x.md; its base name is the slug, and only a read-class buffer is admitted

variables.name: BOXER_SQLAPPLET_WINDOW_SIZE
variables.description: open an applet window at "WxH" logical points (scripted screenshots); empty or unparseable keeps the host's archetype default

variables.name: BOXER_TAB_BASE
variables.description: the URL of the directory a browser tab's page is served from, set by the tab's worker (ADR-0299); a tab binary's prepare step resolves paths against it, and Services.NoEgress lets its origin through

variables.name: BOXER_TAB_HOST_URL
variables.description: base URL a tab binary's `bundle` fetches the Rust browser host from, as <base><sha256>.wasm checked against the digest in browserhost.sum; point it at a mirror or a local directory server for an offline build

variables.name: BOXER_TERRAINSCOPE_POINTS
variables.description: observer and target for a new terrainscope window as four WGS84 decimal degrees, observer latitude, longitude, target latitude, longitude, separated by commas; the sweep starts at once; for scenes and demos

variables.name: BOXER_TINYGO
variables.description: explicit path to the tinygo binary the WASM survey probes are compiled with; the airgap bundle points it at its pinned distribution; empty uses the PATH lookup

variables.name: BOXER_TRAILVIEWER_LOOKBACK
variables.description: how far before an audit event the trail viewer looks for the previous event of the same entity, which its previous-state diff compares against; an entity whose last change is older shows no before-state; at least 1m

variables.name: BOXER_TRAILVIEWER_REFRESH
variables.description: how long an open trail viewer window waits after a read of its case from the trail marts on boxer.facts before the next, in the background; the Refresh button reads at once; under 1s waits a second

variables.name: BOXER_TRAILVIEWER_ROWS
variables.description: how many of the newest rows of its case and window a trail viewer window reads at once; reaching the end of the table reads the next as many; clamped to 100..100000

variables.name: BOXER_TRAIL_REQUIRED
variables.description: refuse a model call whose audit trail rows cannot be written to boxer.facts before the request leaves the machine, and an egress fetch on a host with no durable trail; false lets the work proceed, logged and marked as not durable

variables.name: BOXER_WAIT_FOR_DEBUGGER
variables.description: execution of program waits until an attached debugger is detected (linux only)

variables.name: BOXER_WAVEFORM_DEMO_FILE
variables.description: recording the waveform gallery demo opens at mount, for scripted scenes; empty opens the synthetic track

variables.name: BOXER_WRITINGSTYLESCOPE_DOCS
variables.description: two markdown documents for a new writingstylescope window to compare, as a JSON object {"DocA": ..., "DocB": ...}; the window neither restores nor persists the drafts; for scenes and demos

variables.name: CLICKHOUSE_DATABASE
variables.description: ClickHouse database; consumers omit the X-ClickHouse-Database header when empty

variables.name: CLICKHOUSE_ENDPOINT
variables.description: ClickHouse HTTP endpoint (e.g. http://localhost:8123); tests skip when empty

variables.name: CLICKHOUSE_PASSWORD
variables.description: ClickHouse password; consumers typically omit the auth header when empty

variables.name: CLICKHOUSE_URL
variables.description: ClickHouse HTTP URL used by the play HMI; defaults to localhost

variables.name: CLICKHOUSE_USER
variables.description: ClickHouse user; defaults to the unauthenticated "default" account

variables.name: GEMINI_API_KEY
variables.description: Google AI Studio / Gemini API key

variables.name: GOPATH
variables.description: Go workspace root; empty means $HOME/go applied by the Go toolchain

variables.name: GOROOT
variables.description: Go installation root; empty means consult `go env GOROOT`

variables.name: GOWORK
variables.description: Go workspace file path; "off" disables workspace mode

variables.name: HOME
variables.description: user home directory; supplied by the OS or shell

variables.name: IDS_ACCESSIBILITY
variables.description: accessibility preset overriding Tier-1 palettes: default (honour IDS_PALETTE_*), high-contrast (batlowK + alpha/range boost), monochrome (grayC for sequential, vik fallback for diverging).

variables.name: IDS_PALETTE_DIVERGING
variables.description: user-default diverging palette for signed-deviation charts (delta heatmaps, residual plots). Overridden by IDS_ACCESSIBILITY.

variables.name: IDS_PALETTE_SEQUENTIAL
variables.description: user-default sequential palette for ordered-data charts (boxenplot, treemap, heatmap). All values in the IDS catalogue are perceptually uniform and CVD-safe; the choice is aesthetic. Overridden by IDS_ACCESSIBILITY when that is non-default.

variables.name: IMZERO2_ALLOW_NETWORK
variables.description: set to "1" to allow demo widgets to fetch external resources

variables.name: IMZERO2_BROWSER_TARGET_DIR
variables.description: cargo target directory for building the Rust browser host (rust/imzero2/build_rust_browser.sh, `bundle` of a tab binary); unset is rust/imzero2/target/browser inside boxer, and the user cache directory when bundling from another module, where boxer's sources are read-only

variables.name: IMZERO2_CLIENT_BINARY
variables.description: path to the imzero2 GUI client the host launches; empty speaks the command protocol on stdin/stdout instead of opening a window

variables.name: IMZERO2_COVERAGE_INTERVAL
variables.description: coverage sample interval on -cover -covermode=atomic builds (ADR-0169); a zero or negative duration disables sampling

variables.name: IMZERO2_COVERAGE_TRAIL
variables.description: write Go coverage to the audit trail on -cover -covermode=atomic builds (ADR-0343): the build's function table, the run's covered-set growth, and per agent command the units its handler executed

variables.name: IMZERO2_DENSITY
variables.description: IDS density preset (tight|standard|roomy) at launch, switchable at runtime via the Layout > Density menu; empty defaults to standard

variables.name: IMZERO2_DEPLOY_CURRENT
variables.description: the `current` symlink the demo unit runs through; empty derives <root>/current

variables.name: IMZERO2_DEPLOY_GATE_AUS
variables.description: access units ws_probe must decode for the gate and post-restart health check to pass

variables.name: IMZERO2_DEPLOY_GATE_TIMEOUT
variables.description: overall budget for the gate and the post-restart health probe

variables.name: IMZERO2_DEPLOY_KEEP
variables.description: release dirs to retain for rollback history

variables.name: IMZERO2_DEPLOY_LIVE_PORT
variables.description: the demo service's listen port (post-restart health-probe target)

variables.name: IMZERO2_DEPLOY_RELEASES_DIR
variables.description: immutable release snapshots releases/<tag>/; empty derives <root>/releases

variables.name: IMZERO2_DEPLOY_REMOTE
variables.description: git remote name in the workspace clone (read-only)

variables.name: IMZERO2_DEPLOY_REQUIRE_SIGNED_TAGS
variables.description: verify a tag's GPG/SSH signature (git verify-tag) before building; disable only on a trusted/loopback box

variables.name: IMZERO2_DEPLOY_ROOT
variables.description: on-box deploy root (ADR-0085); workspace/releases/current derive from it unless overridden

variables.name: IMZERO2_DEPLOY_SCRATCH_PORT
variables.description: loopback port the pre-swap gate binds the candidate carrier on

variables.name: IMZERO2_DEPLOY_SERVICE
variables.description: systemd unit restarted on an atomic swap

variables.name: IMZERO2_DEPLOY_WORKSPACE
variables.description: persistent git clone + build caches; empty derives <root>/workspace

variables.name: IMZERO2_DESKTOP_LAYOUT
variables.description: the desktop's layout at launch (ADR-0346): floating, or a tiled layout the window host keeps live — main-stack, tile, columns, rows or monocle; switchable at runtime via Window > Desktop layout; for scenes and demos

variables.name: IMZERO2_FFMPEG_BIN
variables.description: explicit path to the ffmpeg binary the headless encoder, the lane probe and the audio decoder spawn; empty uses the PATH lookup

variables.name: IMZERO2_HEADLESS
variables.description: dual-feature builds only: 1 or on selects the headless host at runtime; ignored in single-host builds

variables.name: IMZERO2_HEADLESS_CODEC
variables.description: startup stream lane: h264 (default; honours ENCODER_ARGS) | vp9 | av1 | av1-444 (AV1 4:4:4) | mesh (ADR-0128 draw-stream, WebGL2 viewer); runtime-switchable from the Go control

variables.name: IMZERO2_HEADLESS_DUMP_DIR
variables.description: directory for per-frame PNG dumps (verification) and for client-requested captures (ADR-0154 CaptureRequest); empty disables both

variables.name: IMZERO2_HEADLESS_DUMP_EVERY
variables.description: with IMZERO2_HEADLESS_DUMP_DIR, dump every Nth frame

variables.name: IMZERO2_HEADLESS_ENCODER_ARGS
variables.description: override ffmpeg encode args between rawvideo input and -f h264 output; empty uses the VAAPI default

variables.name: IMZERO2_HEADLESS_FPS
variables.description: headless render tick in Hz, 1-240; Rust clamps to that range

variables.name: IMZERO2_HEADLESS_H264_OUT
variables.description: append the raw Annex-B H.264 stream to this file (verification); empty disables

variables.name: IMZERO2_HEADLESS_IGNORE_CLOSE
variables.description: truthy makes a UI viewport-close (e.g. a File→Quit item) a no-op instead of a host shutdown; set for a long-lived served deployment so one viewer can't take the host down for everyone

variables.name: IMZERO2_HEADLESS_LISTEN
variables.description: headless carrier bind address host:port (port and port+1 both serve page + WebSocket); empty disables remote access

variables.name: IMZERO2_HEADLESS_MAX_CONNECTIONS
variables.description: max simultaneous viewers on the carrier (ADR-0086 active/passive roster): 1 active + the rest passive; a surplus connection is refused

variables.name: IMZERO2_HEADLESS_MAX_FRAMES
variables.description: stop after N rendered frames (0 = unbounded); smoke-test hook

variables.name: IMZERO2_HEADLESS_PIXELS_PER_POINT
variables.description: initial offscreen HiDPI scale, 0.25-4.0; a connected viewer's devicePixelRatio takes over

variables.name: IMZERO2_HEADLESS_RASTER_STATS
variables.description: log a per-frame raster-cost percentile summary (tessellate + frame into host memory) when the headless host exits; comparable across the wgpu and CPU pixel hosts

variables.name: IMZERO2_HEADLESS_RASTER_THREADS
variables.description: CPU rasterizer worker threads in the headless_soft build; 0 = half the hardware threads (where the measured curve peaks)

variables.name: IMZERO2_MARKDOWN_DEMO_PATH
variables.description: markdown file the widget gallery's markdown demo loads when its window opens; empty starts with nothing loaded

variables.name: IMZERO2_PUFFIN
variables.description: truthy enables the Rust client's puffin scope collection and its loopback profiler server on 127.0.0.1:8585; unset leaves the compiled-in scopes off and the port closed

variables.name: IMZERO2_QUERYRUNS_BACKFILL
variables.description: how far a FIRST-BOOT backfill reaches: all (the source's whole retention), none (start at service start), or a duration such as 24h; ignored once the destination holds facts, so downtime catch-up is unaffected (ADR-0115)

variables.name: IMZERO2_QUERYRUNS_CADENCE
variables.description: refresh cadence of the capture materialized view (whole seconds, minimum 1s); ClickHouse owns the schedule (ADR-0115 SD2)

variables.name: IMZERO2_QUERYRUNS_LISTEN
variables.description: bind address for the queryrunsd /pull endpoint (ADR-0115); must be a loopback host — the refreshable MV reads it via url()

variables.name: IMZERO2_QUERYRUNS_SCOPE
variables.description: capture scope: every terminal query_log event, only boxer-stamped ones, or off (the endpoint serves empty batches)

variables.name: IMZERO2_RENDER_CADENCE
variables.description: frame-loop repaint cadence when idle: continuous (vsync rate) | reactive (idle heartbeat)

variables.name: IMZERO2_RENDER_GOROUTINE_CHECK
variables.description: true: panic when an imzero2 call reaches the FFFI channel off the render loop's goroutine (ADR-0261); costs about a nanosecond per message on amd64 and arm64, microseconds elsewhere

variables.name: IMZERO2_SCREENSHOT_DETERMINISTIC
variables.description: non-empty: skip non-deterministic demos / tours so captures are byte-stable across runs

variables.name: IMZERO2_SCREENSHOT_DIR
variables.description: destination directory for per-window PNG captures; empty disables capture

variables.name: IMZERO2_SCREENSHOT_SIZE
variables.description: tour capture size as WxH (e.g. 1600x900); empty uses per-demo defaults

variables.name: IMZERO2_SYSMETRICS_NATS_URL
variables.description: NATS core URL for the system-metrics plane; when set, consumers subscribe to a standalone sysmetricsd scraper instead of sampling in-process (ADR-0090)

variables.name: IMZERO2_THEME
variables.description: IDS colour theme at launch: dark (the IDS palette, default) | fresh (the light theme of ADR-0258); chosen once per process, not switchable at runtime

variables.name: IMZERO2_WAKE_FIFO
variables.description: set by the host for its client: FIFO the host writes to when the window should run a pass between heartbeats

variables.name: KEELSON_EASTEREGG
variables.description: enable whimsical easter-egg UI flourishes in keelson apps (e.g. the splashscreen colourises its artwork with the viridis palette)

variables.name: KEELSON_INTROSPECT_ENABLE
variables.description: start the keelson introspection HTTP table source in-process (ADR-0094 §SD3); set falsey to disable

variables.name: KEELSON_INTROSPECT_HTTP_LISTEN
variables.description: bind address for the keelson introspection HTTP table source (url() endpoint); must be a loopback host in v1

variables.name: KEELSON_INTROSPECT_SBOM_PATH
variables.description: path to a CycloneDX SBOM JSON exposed as the keelson.sbom introspection table; empty disables the table

variables.name: KEELSON_LAUNCHABLE_APPS_WHERE
variables.description: ClickHouse boolean expression over keelson.apps columns; only apps it selects at boot can be opened, by a person or an agent (ADR-0272). Apps registered later stay launchable. Unset means no limit

variables.name: KEELSON_SERVICES_WHERE
variables.description: ClickHouse boolean expression over keelson.apps columns; the headless apps it selects at boot, among those the launch limit admits, run as services (ADR-0352). Unset means no service runs

variables.name: KEELSON_WATCHBILL_ABANDON_AFTER
variables.description: watchbill worker: a running job whose worker run has no heartbeat this recent is abandoned and re-queued

variables.name: KEELSON_WATCHBILL_ISOLATE_AGENT_JOBS
variables.description: watchbill worker: route a job an agent's call enqueued into the reserved lane that only `watchbill run --job <id>` drains, so it runs in a process of its own (ADR-0344)

variables.name: KEELSON_WATCHBILL_KEEP
variables.description: watchbill worker: finished job rows older than this are deleted; the event rows stay

variables.name: KEELSON_WATCHBILL_LANE_CHILDREN
variables.description: watchbill lane: how many agent-caused jobs run at once, each in a child process of its own (ADR-0344)

variables.name: KEELSON_WATCHBILL_LANE_KILL_GRACE
variables.description: watchbill lane: time a job child has to exit after SIGTERM before it is killed, when the host stops

variables.name: KEELSON_WATCHBILL_POLL
variables.description: watchbill worker: interval between queue reads when no wake arrives

variables.name: LLM_API_KEY
variables.description: API key for non-Gemini LLM providers (LM Studio, generic OpenAI-compatible); prefer the variable to --llm-apikey, which exposes the secret in process argv

variables.name: PEBBLE_MAX_HAMMING_DIST_PER_BYTE_INCL
variables.description: max Hamming distance per byte (inclusive) for anchor matching

variables.name: PEBBLE_N_ANCHOR_BYTES
variables.description: anchor length in bytes for the SkipPastAnchor* fec routines

variables.name: SCCMAP_REPO
variables.description: initial repository path explored by the Repo code exploration app; empty scans the host's worktree

variables.name: SWISSTOPO_TILES_DIR
variables.description: directory containing swissALTI3D 2m COG tiles for the terrainscope app

variables.name: WINDOWHOST_DEBUG_RENDER
variables.description: non-empty enables per-window-body render logging in the windowhost
